newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislator urges moratorium on human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislator urges moratorium on human cloning.

text.p: Spurred by the cloning of a sheep in Scotland, a state legislator Tuesday proposed a five-year moratorium on human cloning in California.

"This is a rational response to the recent scientific discovery in Scotland which may lead the way to human cloning," said state Sen. Patrick Johnston, who introduced a bill proposing the moratorium in the California legislature.

"While there may prove to be beneficial medical applications of some aspects of human cloning research, there are sure to be profound moral, ethical, spiritual, legal and societal implications. This approach provides a period of time sufficient to evaluate those implications," Johnston, a Democrat who chairs the California Senate Select Comittee on Genetics and Public Policy, said in a statement.
Last month Ian Wilmut and colleagues at the Roslin Institute in Edinburgh, Scotland announced they had cloned an adult sheep, the first time an adult animal had been cloned.
The announcement sparked a worldwide furore over whether this could eventually lead to cloning of humans. President Clinton last week banned federally funded human cloning in the United States.

Under Johnston's proposed legislation, which must be approved by the California state legislature and by Republican Gov. Pete Wilson, cloning a human being could bring penalties ranging from $2,500 for the first violation up to $100,000 for a multiple offender.
Offenders could face additional penalties from regulatory authorities, select committee consultant Lisa Matocq said.
